messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT (P2) - Managed cache auth proxy is returning 429s for token verification, causing cache GETs to fallback to origin and rate limiter spikes. Affected: rate-limit service, auth-dependent cache keys, increased tail latency. Pager: @sre-oncall.

sre-oncall: Seen the alerts, getting context. What regions?

maria-lloyd: EU and US-W are noisy. Cloud console shows auth-proxy 502/429s to RedisCloud token validation endpoint.

raj-patel: Noted elevated cache miss rate (x10) across the rate limiter. Current traffic pattern: normal QPS but miss amplification.

oliver-wang: Checking logs, sample trace: ``ERROR auth-proxy: 429 Too Many Requests from rediscloud-auth: /v1/token/verify code=429 retry-after=1`` We are hitting their per-customer token verification limit.

pm-cleo: Customer impact? Any paid customers seeing failed requests?

maria-lloyd: Most customers see higher latencies and occasional 503s from rate-limiter when fallback logic trips. No full account outages yet. Some 3rd-party integrations that rely on strict caching are getting errors.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-445. Triage channel: #inc-1801234567.

raj-patel: Mitigation options: 1) Pause token verification proxy calls and use cached token verdicts for 30s; 2) Route traffic to secondary RedisCloud project (we have a warm peer); 3) Apply client-side exponential backoff and increase local TTLs.

oliver-wang: I can deploy a quick change to the auth middleware to serve cached allow/deny results for 60s (feature flagged). Should reduce calls by ~85%.

sre-oncall: Do that. Maria, can you coordinate the flag and rollout? Keep it canaryed in US-W first.

maria-lloyd: On it. Creating a canary rollout to 5% in US-W. Command: ``/deploy auth-mw --flag auth-cache-short-ttl --canary 5 --region us-west``

oliver-wang: Canary deployed. Observability: token-verification call rate down 70% in canary slice. No errors introduced.

raj-patel: Rate limiter miss rate in canary down to baseline. Good signal. Start ramp to 50% in US-W, 10% in EU.

pm-cleo: Notifying support to prepare customer messages: short note that we are seeing elevated auth-token validation errors from RedisCloud and mitigating with local caching. No need for customer action yet.

maria-lloyd: Ramp done. Monitoring for 10m.

oliver-wang: After ramp, global token-verification calls dropped ~65%, overall tail latency improved ~300ms. Some background jobs still hammering; adding a soft throttle on background job queue.

raj-patel: Also pushed emergency config to rate-limiter: increase fallback capacity (local in-memory tokens) by 2x and reduce strict denial window from 60s -> 10s for the fallback path to avoid client-visible throttles. That'll give breathing room but increases risk of slightly laxer enforcement for a short time.

sre-oncall: Acknowledge. Please log the tradeoff.

pm-cleo: Support message drafted: "We're currently mitigating elevated token verification errors caused by our managed cache provider. We've implemented temporary local caching and throttling changes to reduce customer impact. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary." Approve?

maria-lloyd: Approve. Send.

infra-bot: Support ping sent to #support-team.

oliver-wang: Observability vendor (logstream) also reported ingestion backpressure — could be correlated. I've paused non-essential telemetry from rate-limiter to lower pressure.

raj-patel: Good call. Pressure on the observability pipeline was masking some error spikes; now clearer.

sre-oncall: Is RedisCloud acknowledging?

maria-lloyd: Open ticket with RedisCloud support, they responded: "We're investigating a burst in token-verification traffic from multiple customers; applying mitigation on our side." No ETA yet.

oliver-wang: Next steps: keep auth-cache-ttl flag enabled until their mitigations are verified, keep increased fallback capacity, throttle background jobs, and keep support updates every 30m.

pm-cleo: I'll schedule a 2pm sync with Customer Success for any higher-touch customers.

sre-oncall: Handoff plan: I'm going offline in 40m. @maria-lloyd take primary, @raj-patel secondary. Leave a short summary in the channel when you pick up.

maria-lloyd: Acknowledged. Summary I'll add: what we changed, why, current signals (call rate down 65%, miss rate down to 1.2x baseline), risks (short-term looser enforcement), and follow-ups.

raj-patel: I'll monitor rate-limiter error budget and be ready to rollback the TTL change if we see enforcement regressions.

infra-bot: Reminder: please file postmortem ticket INC-2026-445-PM and add all actions to the incident board.

maria-lloyd: Filed postmortem stub. Action items: (1) Add resilient token-cache in auth proxy with configurable TTL and metrics (owner: oliver), (2) Add automatic adaptive throttling to background job queue (owner: raj), (3) Run chaos test where RedisCloud token endpoint returns 429s for 5m (owner: sre-oncall).

pm-cleo: Thanks team. Will update customers after the next 30m check.

sre-oncall: Handover complete. Leaving in a stable but guarded state. maria-lloyd you are oncall.

maria-lloyd: Taking over. I'll post a short handoff note in 5m with current metrics.

raj-patel: +1, standing by.

infra-bot: Channel archived in 72h unless incident escalates.

maria-lloyd: Handoff note: calls to token-verify: 1200r/s -> 420r/s after mitigations; rate-limiter 95th latency 1.1s -> 0.85s; error rate 5xx -> 0.6% currently. Continuing to monitor.

oliver-wang: Leaving a link to the deploy and logs: https://console.redwood.example/deploys/ab12cd34 and sample logs: ``auth-mw:cache-hit=true token_ttl=60ms``

pm-cleo: Closing loop with support and CS. Will prep a brief postmortem once resolved. :white_check_mark:
